question: ‘Waiting for a Visa’ is a 20-page autobiography written by _____________.
solution:
The correct answer is **Bhimrao Ramji Ambedkar **.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ambedkar** launched the theme of his book, **‘Waiting for a Visa’**, mainly for the profit of foreigners and those who may not be familiar with the concept of untouchability.
 
• The title, “**Waiting for a Visa**,” is metaphorical, a government gives a “Visa” only when the individual is a conventionally approved citizen of a country, and therefore, shows that the country will take complete custody of the safety and safety of that person.
 
• It comprises of memories drawn by Ambedkar, connected to his experiences with untouchability, in his own handwriting. 
 
• The book is served as a textbook at Columbia University.

​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ram Mohan Roy** was an Indian moralist who was one of the originators of the Brahmo Sabha in 1828, the predecessor of the Brahmo Samaj, a social-religious reform movement in the Indian subcontinent.
 
• **Jawahar Lal Nehru** was an Indian anti-colonial nationalist, secular humanist, social democrat, and author who was a chief figure in India in the middle of the 20th century.
 
• **Mahatma Gandhi **was an Indian lawyer, politician, social reformer, and author who became the head of the nationalist movement against the British rule of India.
